2.q: מוֹעֲדֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־תִּקְרְא֥וּ אֹתָ֖⁠ם מִקְרָאֵ֣י קֹ֑דֶשׁ אֵ֥לֶּה הֵ֖ם מוֹעֲדָֽ⁠י
2.note: This verse repeats the phrase **appointed times** for emphasis. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine the phrases and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [These are the special times that Yahweh has set, which you must announce as holy gatherings] or [These are the times that Yahweh has chosen which you must announce for people to gather and worship him]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. See how you translated this abstract noun in 8:9. Alternate translation: [as sacred assemblies] or [as holy gatherings]
Here, **my** refers to Yahweh. Make sure this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [these are Yahweh’s appointed times]

3.note: If your language does not use a passive form like **shall be done**, you could express this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [You may work for six days] or [People may work for six days]

Here, **sabbath of sabbaths** is a common expression emphasizing that this is a very important sabbath. Alternate translation: [is a special sabbath] or [is an especially important sabbath of complete rest]

This phrase refers to everywhere people live, including their homes and the surrounding areas. If your language has a way to express this concept of “everywhere,” consider using it here. Alternate translation: [everywhere you live] or [in all your towns and homes]

4.q: אֵ֚לֶּה מוֹעֲדֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה מִקְרָאֵ֖י קֹ֑דֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־תִּקְרְא֥וּ אֹתָ֖⁠ם בְּ⁠מוֹעֲדָֽ⁠ם
4.note: This verse repeats the phrase **appointed times** for emphasis. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine the phrases and express the emphasis in another way. See how you handled this repetition in 23:2.

5.note: This refers to the first month of the Hebrew calendar, which occurs in March-April on modern calendars. If it would be helpful in your language, you could include this information. Alternate translation: [In the first month of the year, which is in early spring]

Here, **fourteen** is a cardinal number used where many languages would use an ordinal number. If your language would not use a cardinal number in this context, use an ordinal number instead. Alternate translation: [on the fourteenth day of]

The phrase **between the evenings** was a common expression of the culture that meant “at twilight,” which is the time period between sundown and darkness. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [as the sun goes down] or [at dusk]

6.note: Here, **day 15** is a cardinal number used where many languages would use an ordinal number. If your language would not use a cardinal number in this context, use an ordinal number instead. Alternate translation: [And on the fifteenth day of this month]

7.note: These two words **work** and **labor** express a single idea and are used together to emphasize that no work should be done. If your language has a way to emphasize the prohibition of work, you could use it here. Alternate translation: [kind of work] or [work of any kind]

8.note: This phrase means to do something every day for a week. Alternate translation: [each day for seven days] or [every day for a week]

10.note: A **sheaf** is a bundle of grain stalks tied together after being cut. If your language does not have a word for this, you could use a descriptive phrase. Alternate translation: [a bundle of harvested grain stalks from] or [a handful of]

11.note: See how you translated this expression in 1:5. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh] or [in Yahweh’s presence]
See how you translated this abstract noun in 1:3. Alternate translation: [so that Yahweh will accept you] or [so that Yahweh will accept your offering]

12.note: See how you translated this idiom in 9:3. Alternate translation: [one year old] or [that is a year old]

13.note: See how you translated this idiom in 1:9. Alternate translation: [an offering that pleases Yahweh] or [a sacrifice that is acceptable to Yahweh]

The fraction **two-tenths** means two parts out of ten equal parts. Languages handle fractions in different ways. Consider how your language expresses fractions and translate accordingly. Alternate translation: [two parts out of ten of an ephah of] or [one-fifth of an ephah of]

The text only says **two-tenths** but implies that the measurement is in ephahs, which was the standard measure for flour. If your language requires the unit to be stated explicitly, you can include it. Alternate translation: [two-tenths of an ephah of]

An ephah is a Hebrew unit of dry measure, about 22 liters or 20 quarts. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a modern equivalent. Alternate translation: [about 4.4 liters of] or [about 4 quarts of]

The fraction **a fourth of** means one part out of four equal parts. Languages handle fractions in different ways. Consider how your language expresses fractions and translate accordingly. Alternate translation: [one part out of four of a hin] or [a quarter of a hin]

A hin is a Hebrew unit of liquid measure, about 3.8 liters or 1 gallon. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a modern equivalent. Alternate translation: [about 1 liter] or [about 1 quart]

14.note: This phrase uses possession to describe an offering that belongs to God because it is given to him. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the offering that you give to your God] or [the offering that belongs to your God]
See how you translated this phrase in 3:17. Alternate translation: [It is a rule that will continue forever for all your descendants] or [It is a permanent law that all future generations must obey]

15.note: Here, **seven sabbaths** refers to seven weeks, as the sabbath marks the end of each week. Alternate translation: [seven weeks] or [forty-nine days]

16.q: עַ֣ד מִֽ⁠מָּחֳרַ֤ת הַ⁠שַּׁבָּת֙ הַ⁠שְּׁבִיעִ֔ת תִּסְפְּר֖וּ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים י֑וֹם
16.note: This verse clarifies that the fifty days include the seven Sabbaths mentioned in the previous verse. You could say that explicitly if it would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Count fifty days, ending on the day after the seventh Sabbath]

17.note: Here, **dwellings** refers specifically to the homes where people live, not the broader meaning used earlier in the chapter. Alternate translation: [From your homes] or [From each household]
See how you translated this measurement in 23:13.

18.note: See how you translated this common expression in 9:3. Alternate translation: [one-year olds] or [that are a year old]

This phrase may contain extra information that would be unnatural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. See how you translated this expression in 4:3. Alternate translation: [and one young bull]
See how you translated this common expression in 23:13.

19.note: See how you translated this common expression in 23:18.

20.note: Here, **to the face of Yahweh** means to present something directly to Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh] or [in Yahweh’s presence]

21.note: See how you translated this phrase in 23:7.
See how you translated this phrase in 23:14.

22.q: לֹֽא־תְכַלֶּ֞ה פְּאַ֤ת שָֽׂדְ⁠ךָ֙ בְּ⁠קֻצְרֶ֔⁠ךָ וְ⁠לֶ֥קֶט קְצִירְ⁠ךָ֖ לֹ֣א תְלַקֵּ֑ט
22.note: This instruction refers to specific harvesting laws. If it would be helpful in your translation, you could add a footnote explaining the purpose of these practices and referring readers to where it was commanded. See Leviticus 19:9–10 for the full explanation of this law and its purpose. Alternate translation: [do not harvest all the way to the edges of your field, and do not pick up the grain that falls on the ground]

24.note: This refers to the seventh month of the Hebrew calendar, which occurs in September-October on modern calendars. If it would be helpful in your language, you could include this information. Alternate translation: [In the seventh month of the year, which is in early autumn]
If your language would not use a number in a form such as **day one**, you could represent this number in a form your language would use. Alternate translation: [on the first day of the month]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for these concepts, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [a day when you rest from work, shout to remember important events, and gather together to worship in a special way] or [a time for you to stop working, to call out loudly as you recall significant moments, and to come together for a sacred meeting]

25.note: See how you translated this phrase in 23:7.

27.note: See how you translated this abstract noun in 8:9.
See how you translated this expression in 16:29. Alternate translation: [and you shall deny yourselves] or [and you shall fast and pray to show your sadness for your sins]

28.note: See how you translated this expression in 1:5. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh your God] or [in the presence of Yahweh your God]

31.note: See how you translated this phrase in 23:14 and 23:21. This phrase emphasizes the enduring nature of the law. Alternate translation: [It is a rule that will continue forever for all your descendants] or [It is a permanent law that all future generations must obey]

32.note: This is an idiom emphasizing that this is a very important sabbath. Alternate translation: [is a special sabbath] or [is an especially important day of rest]

34.q: בַּ⁠חֲמִשָּׁ֨ה עָשָׂ֜ר י֗וֹם לַ⁠חֹ֤דֶשׁ הַ⁠שְּׁבִיעִי֙ הַ⁠זֶּ֔ה
34.note: If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **day 15**, you could represent this number in a form your language would use. Alternate translation: [On the fifteenth day of this seventh month]

36.note: This phrase means to do something every day for a week. See how you translated this in 23:8. Alternate translation: [Each day for seven days] or [Every day for a week]
See how you translated this phrase in 23:2.

37.note: This is a common expression that means to do what is required each day. Alternate translation: [as each day requires] or [what needs to be done on each specific day]

38.q: מִ⁠לְּ⁠בַ֖ד שַׁבְּתֹ֣ת יְּהוָ֑ה וּ⁠מִ⁠לְּ⁠בַ֣ד מַתְּנֽוֹתֵי⁠כֶ֗ם וּ⁠מִ⁠לְּ⁠בַ֤ד כָּל־נִדְרֵי⁠כֶם֙ וּ⁠מִ⁠לְּ⁠בַד֙ כָּל־נִדְב֣וֹתֵי⁠כֶ֔ם
38.note: This verse lists several types of offerings that are in addition to the regular festival offerings. If your language has a way to express items in a list that are additional to something else, you could use it here. Alternate translation: [in addition to your regular Sabbath offerings, your other gifts, your vows, and your freewill offerings]

39.note: If your language would not represent a number using the form **day 15**, you could represent this number in a form your language would use. Alternate translation: [on the fifteenth day of the seventh month]

See how you translated this phrase in 23:8. Alternate translation: [each day for seven days] or [every day for a week]

43.note: Here, **sons of Israel** refers to the Israelite people who came out of Egypt. This represents all the Israelite people by referring to them as sons. Alternate translation: [the Israelite people] or [the people of Israel]

This verse explains why God commanded the people to live in booths during the festival. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this connection more explicit. Alternate translation: [I commanded this so that all your descendants would remember]
